verdict.rationale: Cursor's Cloud Agents clearly open pull requests: they open PRs in the repos they change, support branch/PR targeting with `autoCreatePR`, verify work before pushing a PR, and report the target `branchName` and `prUrl` in webhook payloads. The evidence never explicitly documents the agent staging changes or writing commit messages, and branch creation is only implied. missing for 10: explicit documentation of staging changes, agent-authored commit messages, an explicit branch-creation workflow in the local IDE/CLI agent, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent stage changes, write commit messages, create branches, and open pull requests

citations.quote: inspect the full workspace, make coordinated changes, and open pull requests in the repos it changes
Agents can start dev servers, open the app in a browser, click through UI flows, and verify their changes work before pushing a PR.
a JSON payload carrying repository/ref source, target url/branchName/prUrl, and a summary
